source: The ceramic prize rules say entrants must be “members living within twelve miles of the studio.” Noor has a flat eight miles away and a room near her job twenty miles away. She stays at the room on working nights and at the flat most weekends. Her membership is current. The rules do not define living within the area, name a particular address record, or say whether someone can have more than one residence. Last year's organiser accepted an entrant who spent the winter elsewhere, but we do not know what address or circumstances that entrant supplied. This year's organiser has asked for a plain explanation of the rule before answering Noor. The committee has not discussed her situation, and the entry form only asks for a contact address. Noor wants to know whether she can enter before preparing photographs of her work.
objective: Rewrite the residency rule so Noor gets an unambiguous yes or no about eligibility. Use the existing rule and details here without adding a new policy condition.

items.text:
The ceramic prize is open to “members living within twelve miles of the studio.” Noor's membership is current. She has a flat eight miles away, where she stays most weekends, and a room near her job twenty miles away, where she stays on working nights.

The existing rule does not give an unambiguous yes or no about her eligibility. It does not define what counts as living within the area, specify an address record, or say how multiple residences are treated. The entry form asks only for a contact address.

Last year's organiser accepted an entrant who spent the winter elsewhere, but we do not know the address or circumstances that entrant supplied, so that example does not resolve Noor's case. The committee has not discussed her situation. This year's organiser has requested a plain explanation before answering her, but deciding her eligibility requires a clarification of the rule that the supplied information does not provide. Noor is waiting for an answer before preparing photographs of her work.
